Gold fell to $4,307.50 Wednesday morning, the fifth straight lower mark since Friday 28 August, and platinum and silver fell further still.

Platinum is down $170.00 or 9.03% and silver 9.68% to $63.56 over the same five marks, both losing more than gold's 6.45%. The gold-silver ratio widened to 67.77 from 65.43, a sign the trade sold the whole complex rather than one metal.

Platinum fell 1.38% to $1,713.00 Wednesday, the sharpest single-session move of the four metals, though gold has lost the least since Friday.

Gold slipped 0.47% to $4,307.50, silver 0.62% to $63.56 and palladium 0.08% to $1,286.00, the fifth straight lower reading for gold and platinum since 28 August. Platinum is now down 9.03% over that run and silver 9.68%, both worse than gold's 6.45%.
